analysis: The code snippet has two substring calls: `nodeString.substring(0,lastIdx)` (two-argument) and `nodeString.substring(lastIdx + separateStr.length())` (one-argument). Before these calls, the code checks `if (lastIdx == -1)` and throws an IllegalArgumentException if true, ensuring that `lastIdx` is at least 0 and that `separateStr` exists in `nodeString`. For the first call: beginIndex=0 (non-negative), endIndex=lastIdx (which is between 0 and nodeString.length()-1), so 0 <= endIndex <= length-1 < length, and beginIndex <= endIndex, satisfying all conditions. For the second call: beginIndex = lastIdx + separateStr.length(). Since `lastIdx` is the start of the last occurrence of `separateStr`, we have lastIdx + separateStr.length() <= nodeString.length() (if `separateStr` is at the end, equality holds). Also lastIdx >= 0, so beginIndex >= separateStr.length() > 0 (assuming separateStr non-empty; even if empty, lastIndexOf returns length, so beginIndex = length, valid). Thus beginIndex is within [0, length]. Therefore, the throwing conditions for IndexOutOfBoundsException (negative beginIndex, endIndex > length, beginIndex > endIndex for two-argument; negative or > length for one-argument) are all avoided by the prior validation and the properties of lastIndexOf.
remark: The only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException. In this context, the condition `lastIdx != -1` guarantees that `lastIdx` is a valid index, so `substring(0, lastIdx)` always has beginIndex=0 <= endIndex=lastIdx < length, and `substring(lastIdx + separateStr.length())` has beginIndex between separateStr.length() and length inclusive, both satisfying the bounds. Thus no IndexOutOfBoundsException can be triggered.
